subject.title: fix: gateway kill leaves Codex tool processes running

question: What Windows process-tree ownership contract must Gateway hard cancellation support before this PR can merge?
rationale: The code cannot simultaneously prove descendant exit, avoid targeting a reused PID, and safely retain cancellation ownership after the root exits without an explicit platform ownership primitive or a maintainer-approved degraded contract.

options.title: Add durable Windows ownership
options.body: Create a spawn-time Job Object or equivalent durable tree handle, use it for cancellation and exit proof, and release the scope only after the owned tree is confirmed empty.

options.title: Narrow the strict Windows path
options.body: Keep the POSIX/macOS strict drain but preserve the existing Windows behavior until a separately reviewed durable ownership implementation is available.

options.title: Accept fail-closed retention
options.body: Merge with the known possibility that an exited Windows root permanently blocks run-id reuse and later drains when descendants cannot be proven dead.

recommendation.title: Add durable Windows ownership
recommendation.body: Create a spawn-time Job Object or equivalent durable tree handle, use it for cancellation and exit proof, and release the scope only after the owned tree is confirmed empty.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history spans both the shared supervisor and Codex app-server lifecycle surfaces involved in the platform contract.
